 Foley Plans Month Of Holiday Events For Families This December
 OBA Staff • November 21, 2026 
 Six free or low-cost events run from Dec. 4th through Dec. 20th 
 Foley, Ala. — ( OBA ) —  The City of Foley has lined up a full month of holiday events for residents and visitors of all ages. The schedule runs from early to late December and includes everything from a community tree lighting to a lighted nature trail. Mayor Ralph Hellmich said the season brings the whole community together, from school choirs and bands to local businesses and civic clubs. Most events are free. 
The first event, Christmas in the Park, is scheduled for Friday, Dec. 4, from 6 to 8 p.m. at Heritage Park, 101 E. Laurel Ave. The Mathis Elementary School choir and the Senior Center Bells will perform, and Santa and Mrs. Claus will make an appearance. Free hot chocolate and goodies will be served, and winners of the Christmas Tree Decorating Contest will be announced. 
That same evening, the Mobile Symphony Youth Orchestra will perform a holiday concert at the Foley Civic Center, 407 E. Laurel Ave., on Friday, Dec. 4, from 7 to 8 p.m. A $5 donation is suggested for the concert. The orchestra features young musicians performing holiday music. 
The weekend continues Saturday, Dec. 5, with the Foley Kiwanis Christmas Parade at 10 a.m. in downtown Foley. Floats, marching groups, and holiday music will fill the streets. Families can catch candy along the route and watch for Santa Claus. 
Right after the parade, Let It Snow kicks off at Heritage Park on Saturday, Dec. 5, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. The event features arts and crafts, face painting, a snowflake scavenger hunt, camel rides, a petting zoo, and Whoville hair styling. Performers include the Foley High School band, Baldwin Baddies, Annabella, and Coastal Dance Company. Concessions will be available, and admission is free. 
The Graham Creek Christmas Trail brings the holiday spirit to Graham Creek Nature Preserve at 23030 Wolf Bay Drive. Visitors can stroll along a decorated trail and boardwalk lit with Christmas lights and themed displays. Santa and the Snow Princesses will greet guests. Admission is $5 per person, with children two and younger admitted free. 
The trail runs over three separate weekends: 
Saturday, Dec. 5, 5 to 8 p.m. 
 Friday–Sunday, Dec. 11–13, 5 to 8 p.m. 
 Friday–Sunday, Dec. 18–20, 5 to 8 p.m. 
The Christmas Night Market rounds out the schedule on Thursday, Dec. 10, from 4 to 8 p.m. at the Coastal Alabama Farmers and Fishermens Market, 781 Farmer Market Lane. Shoppers can browse gifts from local artisans, pick up Christmas treats from local bakers, and enjoy food trucks, holiday music, and children's activities. Santa will also stop by. 
"The holidays are an extremely special time in Foley," Hellmich said. "These events are what make Christmas in Foley feel like home. The whole community comes out for them, from our school choirs and bands to our local businesses and civic clubs. We invite everyone to join us, make some memories and celebrate the season together." 
For more information about City of Foley events, visit CityofFoley.org . A complete listing of holiday events, including those at local businesses and restaurants, is available on VisitFoley.com .
